_comment: THE CATALOGUE SOURCE. A human edits this file; git reviews it; the seed
script pushes it into Firestore. NOTHING reads it at runtime — the
functions and the client read Firestore, which this file defines.
What lives here is AUTHORITY plus the text needed to name a thing:
price, slot, sellable, unavailable, name, sub. What does NOT live here
is art — emoji and gradient stay in the app keyed by itemId, because the
RENDERER ships in the app too. Moving art would not buy the ability to
add an item without a release; it would buy the ability to SELL one that
cannot be delivered, which is the sticker pack all over again.
Withdrawn items stay here as tombstones. A catalogue that cannot name an
id appearing in its own ledger and inventory documents is broken, and
the raw slug in My Items is what that looks like from the outside.
dailyTasks says what a task PAYS and how much of it is needed. Which
tasks EXIST is the server's to decide (TASK_VERIFIERS in functions/
index.js): a row here with no verifier is refused, never paid on trust.
